scope: Player-facing semantic object roles across the supplied 276 games.
method: Source tags and authored/initialized level snapshots, supplemented by reviewed dynamic, implicit, UI and composite-object roles. This is an analysis taxonomy, not an engine class enumeration or a trained detector.
limitations: A role can be implicit background, a region, a UI element or a composite of sprites. One object may have several roles.
Per-game role lists describe the supplied game family. They do not assert that every role appears in every level or every frame.
Some game code supports tags not instantiated in the supplied snapshots. Presence inferred from source is not proof of a visible instance in every level.
Snapshots record the initialized first level and authored later levels. Static palette values and visibility can change at runtime.
Global appearance/color rules are insufficient. Hidden state and behavior can be required to distinguish objects.
Baseline scene attributes (identity, position, shape/mask, color, orientation, scale, visibility, occupancy, relations and state history) apply across types.

types.recognition_cues: The body whose movement or edit responds to the active controls. Color alone is insufficient.
types.track: Identity; occupied mask; position; orientation; selected state; size; carried item
types.role: Move it, protect it, and associate it with its own goal.

types.recognition_cues: A second body that follows, mirrors, shares commands, or can swap with the player.
types.track: Stable identity; controller; movement coupling; own goal; offset from leader
types.role: Coordinate its route with the player; some games require both bodies at goals.

types.recognition_cues: Repeated connected or ordered bodies trailing a head.
types.track: Segment order; predecessor; previous positions; length; collision occupancy
types.role: Keep the chain clear and distinguish the head from its dependent segments.

types.recognition_cues: A duplicate body whose behavior depends on past moves, reflection, or split state.
types.track: Original identity; replay index; path; phase; sign-flipped control; active/paired state
types.role: Use or reunite copies; identical appearance does not imply independent control.

types.recognition_cues: A nonplayer body that updates according to scent or another local rule.
types.track: Position; heading; sensed field; update order; destination
types.role: Guide it indirectly rather than assuming it is the controllable avatar.

types.recognition_cues: A body that pursues, patrols, reacts, or creates collision danger.
types.track: Identity; position; facing; route; speed; update phase; behavior subtype
types.role: Predict its next move and avoid or redirect it.

types.recognition_cues: A body that can attach to, carry, and drop another object.
types.track: Helpful/opposing role; cargo link; heading; destination; combined footprint
types.role: Coordinate helpful carriers and stop opponents taking cargo away.

types.recognition_cues: A target that appears in a hole or lane for a limited interval.
types.track: Active slot; remaining visibility; lane; already-hit state; decoy status
types.role: Click the active genuine target before it disappears.

types.recognition_cues: The playable space between obstacles; it may be implicit background rather than a sprite.
types.track: Bounds; occupancy; walkability; friction; visit count; entry cost
types.role: Find legal routes and infer global ice or timing rules from movement.

types.recognition_cues: A solid boundary or obstacle that blocks an attempted action.
types.track: Occupied mask; connectivity; line-of-sight blocking; fixed position
types.role: Plan around its full footprint, including corners and narrow passages.

types.recognition_cues: A barrier whose collision state depends on a key, hue, plane, timeline, or switch.
types.track: Open/closed; required key/color/phase; linked control; temporary/permanent opening
types.role: Recognize its current state and the condition needed to pass.

types.recognition_cues: A barrier that shifts when pushed, selected, or advanced by time.
types.track: Position; motion axis; phase; selectable state; occupied destination
types.role: Use it to reshape the route without trapping or crushing a body.

types.recognition_cues: A blocking tile with a destruction interaction or distinct weak-wall appearance.
types.track: Intact/broken; drill/dig/blast requirement; remaining tool budget
types.role: Remove the relevant barrier while preserving the action budget.

types.recognition_cues: A supporting surface, sometimes carried or translated as a whole with its contents.
types.track: Support relation; extent; movable axis; attached objects; enabled state
types.role: Keep bodies supported and account for everything carried by a moving floor.

types.recognition_cues: An unwalkable or lethal gap between reachable regions.
types.track: Mask; crossing length; bridge eligibility; water versus fatal gap
types.role: Build a legal crossing or route around it.

types.recognition_cues: A placed or movable crossing that makes part of a gap traversable.
types.track: Endpoints; covered cells; length; remaining lifetime; disappears-on-leave flag
types.role: Cross before it vanishes and distinguish the bridge from the gap beneath it.

types.recognition_cues: A fixed post or socket used as a connection endpoint.
types.track: Position; partner; distance/alignment; attachment status
types.role: Choose compatible endpoints for ropes, bridges, or supported assemblies.

types.recognition_cues: An arrow or marked lane imposes an additional, next-turn, or package movement.
types.track: Arrow vector; pending vector; destination-cell trigger; rotation; payload
types.role: Predict forced movement; different games consume arrow effects at different times.

types.recognition_cues: A marked region relocates a body when entered.
types.track: Source/destination pairing; directionality; displacement; remaining uses
types.role: Identify which direction works and whether the link is consumed.

types.recognition_cues: A marked tile changes heading or extends movement.
types.track: Heading change; jump delta; landing cell; trigger timing
types.role: Predict the actual landing cell, not just the entered tile.

types.recognition_cues: A floor tile changes state after visits, departure, or elapsed turns.
types.track: Visit count; cracked/collapsed; first-visit time; expiry; underlying hole
types.role: Plan the remaining route before consuming a tile’s safe uses.

types.recognition_cues: A deposited trace persists or decays, sometimes visible only as tint or inferred from actions.
types.track: Owner; age; deposit event; visit count; blocking/lethal/attracting role; intensity
types.role: Distinguish harmless history, blocking ink, detectable scent and an attractive pheromone gradient.

types.recognition_cues: A brown or otherwise marked cell may stop a sliding crate or block the player.
types.track: Game-specific collision role; stopping behavior; removable state
types.role: Use it as a brake where allowed; do not transfer its meaning between games.

types.recognition_cues: A region changes an object’s color, shape, rotation, size, aura, or split state.
types.track: Region mask; transformation; affected attributes; linked state; entry event
types.role: Pass through the right sequence of regions to acquire the required state.

types.recognition_cues: A pad or station replenishes a meter, grants steps, or provides temporary immunity.
types.track: Resource type; amount; cap; one-use/reusable; automatic versus ACTION5 activation
types.role: Compare its benefit with the detour and required interaction.

types.recognition_cues: A region protects a particular survival resource while occupied.
types.track: Shelter type; containment; entry order; protected resource
types.role: Choose the right shelter and obey any alternating-entry rule.

types.recognition_cues: A marked heat source or editable heater pad affects the local temperature field.
types.track: On/off; emission; affected neighbors; temperature; probe location
types.role: Predict field updates and whether the target cells can receive heat.

types.recognition_cues: A region gains neighboring cells over successive updates.
types.track: Type; frontier; spread rule; cadence; lethal versus blocking; immunity interaction
types.role: Keep an escape corridor and distinguish spreading terrain from moving actors.

types.recognition_cues: A placed cell blocks further expansion of fire or infection.
types.track: Position; blocked spread edges; permanence; placement budget
types.role: Cut the dangerous expansion route or steer a strain’s growth.

types.recognition_cues: Connected cells share a team, color, or strain and expand from seeds.
types.track: Owner; active strain; frontier; area; adjacency; rival occupancy
types.role: Grow a qualifying region to the required count.

types.recognition_cues: A danger marker or barrier has a collision rule that may block, damage, or end the run.
types.track: Mask; collision rule; damage; passability versus lethality
types.role: Avoid its contact area; some red-looking objects merely block instead.

types.recognition_cues: A row, mask, or gate cycles between dangerous and safe states.
types.track: Period; phase; offset; next active mask; immunity interval
types.role: Time crossings from the actual safe phase.

types.recognition_cues: A discrete body falls when its next support cell is clear.
types.track: Position; support; gravity direction; next fall; crushing area
types.role: Anticipate the fall after movement or terrain edits.

types.recognition_cues: A pushable or timed object triggers an area or directional explosion.
types.track: Fuse; blast mask; propagation direction; affected weak walls; chain reaction
types.role: Get clear before detonation and use the blast deliberately.

types.recognition_cues: A moving point, ray, or front progresses in a direction and reacts to obstacles.
types.track: Heading; occupied path; update step; reflection; branching; target hit
types.role: Trace every collision before advancing or releasing it.

types.recognition_cues: A lethal location can look identical to a safe floor cell.
types.track: Coordinate; revealed state; clue constraints; known/unknown status
types.role: Infer safety from clues or the reference map; appearance alone may not identify it.

types.recognition_cues: A target-like object has a wrong-goal, wrong-lane, forbidden-color, or penalty role.
types.track: True/false target role; color; lane; current rule; penalty
types.role: Reject it even when its shape resembles a valid target.

types.recognition_cues: A designated cell or region is the required arrival location.
types.track: Position/mask; assigned body; prerequisites; hold count; moving/static
types.role: Reach it in the required state; touching it may be insufficient.

types.recognition_cues: An intermediate marked location must be visited or traversed.
types.track: Visited state; order; entry direction; required number; belongs-to path
types.role: Include it in the route before the final goal.

types.recognition_cues: A marker specifies where a crate, peg, endpoint, or transformed piece belongs.
types.track: Expected type/color/shape; target mask; occupied status; matching object
types.role: Match the right object and required attributes to the target.

types.recognition_cues: A terminal accepts a beam, pulse, flow, grains, or a delivered package.
types.track: Required/forbidden; input direction; filled/lit; capacity; accepted material
types.role: Feed all required receivers while avoiding forbidden ones.

types.recognition_cues: A region or customer accepts cargo or counts contained objects.
types.track: Required owner/color/type/count; containment; attached/detached; deadline
types.role: Deliver the correct object, explicitly release it where required, and meet quotas.

types.recognition_cues: A removable item or token affects completion when touched or clicked.
types.track: Identity; color/value; required order; collectible-now flag; remaining set
types.role: Collect only under the active color/order rule.

types.recognition_cues: A collectible is linked to a door, or must remain tethered near the player.
types.track: Key identity; linked door; acquired state; leash; prerequisites for appearance
types.role: Match keys to doors and distinguish an inventory key from a tethered object.

types.recognition_cues: An item replenishes hunger or lengthens a snake after collection.
types.track: Position; consumed state; resource amount; growth effect
types.role: Schedule collection before starvation or self-blocking growth.

types.recognition_cues: A transferable object has a destination, order, or delivery behavior.
types.track: Identity; color/kind; destination; carrier; deadline; pickup/drop state
types.role: Transport and release the correct item without mixing up orders.

types.recognition_cues: A solid movable object responds to push, pull, magnetism, or a winch.
types.track: Position; footprint; color; weight; push count; sliding; target match
types.role: Preserve access for the next push/pull and avoid irreversible traps.

types.recognition_cues: Two or more occupied cells move as one rigid object.
types.track: Identity across cells; extent; permitted displacement; exit-lane occupancy
types.role: Check the whole destination footprint before pushing.

types.recognition_cues: A connected pixel mask can translate, rotate, recolor, or deform.
types.track: Mask; holes; orientation; color; scale; selected state; reflection copies
types.role: Match geometric occupancy or target pixels using the game’s actual comparison.

types.recognition_cues: A piece can jump a neighboring peg onto a valid empty landing.
types.track: Position; exact type/color; counted status; floor support; legal landing
types.role: Use matching-type jumps to remove pegs and other types as stepping stones.

types.recognition_cues: A sized horizontal piece belongs to an ordered stack on a peg.
types.track: Size; peg; vertical order; held state; larger/smaller relation
types.role: Move top disks without placing a larger disk on a smaller one.

types.recognition_cues: A fruit sprite has a tier and can combine with equal-tier fruit.
types.track: Tier; position; equal-tier groups; merger result; collision compatibility
types.role: Merge only compatible fruit and keep the requested tier counts.

types.recognition_cues: Connected segments rotate or change length and carry descendants.
types.track: Parent/child links; pivot; length; angle; swept mask; endpoint
types.role: Adjust parent joints with their downstream effects in mind.

types.recognition_cues: Selectable small supports position a larger associated body.
types.track: Belongs-to body; center; allowed positions; number of supports
types.role: Move supports to control the body’s centroid without hitting hazards.

types.recognition_cues: A central shape follows the average position of its support centers.
types.track: Support set; integer centroid; mask; matching goal; swept path
types.role: Recognize the assembly as one mechanism and match its central body.

types.recognition_cues: A geometric track carries an ordered sequence or cycles pieces around a loop.
types.track: Length; orientation; connector; position order; carried colors; paired reference
types.role: Modify the track or cycle it while preserving the required order.

types.recognition_cues: Parallel lanes have adjustable lengths and swappable contents.
types.track: Lane association; length; token order/color; boundary positions; paired control
types.role: Align each token with the correct goal on the correct lane.

types.recognition_cues: A marked cell or button changes linked geometry or activation state.
types.track: Activated state; linked door; weight threshold; required count; one-use/reversible
types.role: Determine what activates it and which objects it controls.

types.recognition_cues: Connected cells or segments conduct according to direction and turn rules.
types.track: Endpoints; incoming/outgoing direction; junction turn restrictions; on/off
types.role: Build and trace a valid path through the network.

types.recognition_cues: An oriented segment exposes a set of connection ports.
types.track: H/V/T/cross; orientation; open ports; connected neighbors
types.role: Join compatible ports from source to sink.

types.recognition_cues: An oriented slash, backslash, or barrier redirects a beam or flow.
types.track: Orientation; incoming/outgoing vector; fragile/durable; editable/movable
types.role: Predict the reflected path and whether use consumes the piece.

types.recognition_cues: A connection node passes a pulse, sometimes resetting its hop depth.
types.track: On/off; adjacency; reachable state; amplifier flag; depth reset
types.role: Connect the source to lamps within the pulse-depth limit.

types.recognition_cues: A starting point launches a beam, bolt, pulse, or directional flow.
types.track: Position; facing; emitted type; release/test control; movable state
types.role: Begin tracing at its actual first emitted cell and heading.

types.recognition_cues: A selectable node is incident to abstract edges.
types.track: Identity; selected state; incident edges; selection budget
types.role: Choose vertices that cover every required edge.

types.recognition_cues: A relation connects two cells or graph nodes; it is not simply filled area.
types.track: Endpoint identities; selected/covered; unit adjacency; path membership
types.role: Cover or claim the listed relation using its two endpoints.

types.recognition_cues: A toggleable cell determines whether two regions remain connected.
types.track: Open/closed; reachable components; source-target connectivity
types.role: Close a cut that disconnects S from T.

types.recognition_cues: A separate mechanism pulls or attaches to a movable object.
types.track: Anchor; facing; reach; selected cargo; attached/released; control mapping
types.role: Operate the mechanism while tracking the carried object and player separately.

types.recognition_cues: A line defines a geometric reflection, sometimes itself movable.
types.track: Axis position; orientation; fixed/movable; linked shapes; reflection transform
types.role: Relate source and reflected coordinates correctly.

types.recognition_cues: An icon or labeled region invokes a discrete operation such as run, swap, transfer, rotate, or select.
types.track: Hitbox; command; target object/group; enabled state; cost
types.role: Recognize the control separately from its illustration or target.

types.recognition_cues: A border, cursor, tab, or tumbler determines which object or operation receives input.
types.track: Selected identity; active row/column/layer/peg/routine; current value
types.role: Keep the active selection and mode explicit before each edit.

types.recognition_cues: A placed light source exposes hidden cells in a neighborhood.
types.track: Position; reveal metric; radius; remaining placements; shrinking rule
types.role: Reveal useful locations before making irreversible guesses.

types.recognition_cues: A cell changes between empty and colored states after a click or stamp.
types.track: Coordinate; color/state; editable status; goal membership; component count
types.role: Match the required state and distinguish erase-only from toggle/cycle behavior.

types.recognition_cues: A closed outline contains an interior handled as a whole by one click.
types.track: Boundary; interior; connected component; filled/erased; hint cells
types.role: Click inside the correct enclosure and track the entire region’s state.

types.recognition_cues: A mask specifies the group of cells affected by one action.
types.track: Mask; anchor; orientation; paint color; overwrite/union/toggle behavior
types.role: Predict the complete edit footprint before applying it.

types.object_type: Reference pattern / target image / target icon
types.recognition_cues: A read-only panel or icon shows the state the editable board should attain.
types.track: Mask; orientation; color; scale; required versus ignored pixels; correspondence
types.role: Compare the correct target with the correct working object or panel.

types.recognition_cues: A tile contains an arrow, L, T, cross, corner, or colored subpattern.
types.track: Identity; exact pixel mask; orientation; rotation symmetry; row/column coupling
types.role: Match its observable pattern; symmetric rotations may be indistinguishable.

types.recognition_cues: A numbered tile occupies one cell next to a distinguished blank.
types.track: Tile identity; position; blank location; target permutation
types.role: Move the blank to permute tiles without losing solved positions.

types.recognition_cues: An editable binary cell changes together with its influence neighborhood.
types.track: On/off; click kernel; wrap rules; wall exclusion
types.role: Track XOR changes and leave every light off.

types.recognition_cues: A binary population evolves by neighbor counts on explicit advances.
types.track: Live set; neighborhood; torus/bounded edges; generation count; target
types.role: Recognize both the current population and the required generation.

types.recognition_cues: A cell or row entry stores a small modular value encoded by color.
types.track: Value; modulus; neighbors; global update operator; target coordinates
types.role: Apply the actual sum, product, or XOR rule instead of guessing from hue.

types.recognition_cues: A spatial temperature field or probe reading changes under heating, cooling or diffusion.
types.track: Temperature per cell; source neighborhood; diffusion rule; probe coordinate; allowed band
types.role: Relate heat sources to the probe or required region; color represents a numeric state.

types.recognition_cues: A grid cell contains an integer quantity that topples at a threshold.
types.track: Grain count; threshold; adjacent sinks/walls; stable state; total
types.role: Count retained grains and distinguish this simulation from falling sand bodies.

types.recognition_cues: A facedown tile reveals a color when selected.
types.track: Persistent slot identity; remembered color; face state; pair/triple membership; match state
types.role: Remember identities across concealment and match the required group size.

types.recognition_cues: A discrete colored symbol appears in an ordered cue or response area.
types.track: Symbol identity; queue membership; index; visible/hidden; pending double tap
types.role: Choose the correct next symbol and preserve each queue’s ordering.

types.recognition_cues: A token or editable bit belongs to an executable command pattern.
types.track: Operation; position; on/off; operand; current execution index; available spell
types.role: Build the intended command sequence or exact recognition mask.

types.recognition_cues: An ordered group of instructions can be selected or called by another routine.
types.track: Routine identity; instruction slots; call links; return stack; execution position
types.role: Recognize reusable groups and their control flow, not just individual colors.

types.recognition_cues: A visible mapping substitutes one symbol or string for another.
types.track: Left/right sides; rule order; current string; mutable output/rule slots
types.role: Predict the full rewritten sequence before committing the rule.

types.recognition_cues: A signed variable belongs to one or more OR clauses.
types.track: Variable identity; polarity; truth value; clauses sharing the variable
types.role: Toggle the variable while preserving satisfaction of the other clauses.

types.recognition_cues: A labeled circuit element has a selectable numeric resistance.
types.track: Ohms; branch; position; editable/fixed; linked node voltages
types.role: Recognize connectivity and value; compute the exact target voltages.

types.recognition_cues: A distinguished empty location can receive a tile, peg, or instruction.
types.track: Position; occupied/empty; accepted type; required adjacency; active highlight
types.role: Preserve valid landing space and distinguish an empty slot from outside the board.

types.recognition_cues: A symbol constrains nearby cells, colors, runs, or hidden mines.
types.track: Reference color/value; neighbor offsets; equality/inequality; row/column association
types.role: Interpret the clue under this game’s rule and solve the constraints together.

types.object_type: Pairing marker / endpoint / small target pixel
types.recognition_cues: A small dot or subpixel marks a piece’s alignment point or a path endpoint.
types.track: Belongs-to piece; type; exact coordinate; pairing; multiplicity
types.role: Track markers inside composite pieces and do not merge different hidden types.

types.recognition_cues: A legend or signpost shows available, safe, forbidden, or target colors.
types.track: Color-to-role mapping; current selection; forbidden color; cycle phase
types.role: Use the current legend; the same hue can have different meanings in another game.

types.recognition_cues: A separate panel encodes the contents of another uniform-looking grid.
types.track: Panel bounds; row/column correspondence; safe/mine labels; player location
types.role: Map coordinates across panels without mistaking the map itself for the playfield.

types.recognition_cues: A required location is concealed until a reveal action or beacon reaches it.
types.track: Known/unknown; revealed set; underlying target; reveal history
types.role: Separate what is visible from what is logically known.

types.recognition_cues: An overlay records a guess, choice, visit, or completed target.
types.track: Marked identity; semantic meaning; correctness; persistent/transient; underlying object
types.role: Treat the overlay as state on an object or cell, not a replacement for its identity.

types.recognition_cues: A bar, ticks, icons, or number summarizes a resource or progress count.
types.track: Value; cap; remaining lives/actions; score threshold; what consumes/refills it
types.role: Read the limit that can invalidate an otherwise correct plan.

types.recognition_cues: A moving cursor, charge bar, phase marker, or countdown changes on updates.
types.track: Current phase; period; direction; charge; success hold; update clock
types.role: Relate visible progress to action steps and know when to wait, hold, or act.

types.recognition_cues: A border or separator partitions input, output, legend, and control areas.
types.track: Panel role; bounds; scale; coordinate transform; clipping/padding
types.role: Do not confuse a reference or control panel with editable board cells.

If the player starts on waypoint 0, that one counts as already visited. next_level() runs right after you step onto the last waypoint. Yellow marks show the route; each completed waypoint turns green; floor you walked is also tinted green (trail). Step budget (step_limit = shortest solve in successful moves): each successful move uses one step. Hitting OOB or a wall does not move you and does not spend a step. You lose if you use all step_limit successful moves without clearing the route — the winning move must be the last budgeted step onto the final waypoint.
